text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on February 28 in history.
1784 - John Wesley signed the "deed of declaration" formalising the establishment of the Wesleyan faith, or Methodists.
1824 - Blondin, pseudonym of Jean-Francois Gravelet, French tightrope walker who made several crossings of the Niagra Falls, born.
1825 - A treaty was signed between Britain and Russia settling the border between Canada and Alaska, then a Russia possession.
1844 - On the Potomac River the U.S. navy was demonstrating its new frigate "Princeton" when one of its guns exploded, killing the Secretary of State, Navy Secretary and other government officials.
1900 - In the Boer War, Ladysmith was relieved by General Redvers Buller.
1901 - Professor Linus Pauling, U.S. chemist and physicist, born. In 1954 he won the Nobel prize for chemistry and in 1962 the Nobel Peace Prize.
1913 - Vincente Minnelli, U.S. film director, born. He won several Oscars for his musicals in the 1950s and his marriage to Judy Garland produced a daughter, Liza Minnelli.
1916 - Henry James, American novelist, died in England.
1921 - Russia and Afghanistan signed a treaty of friendship providing political and financial aid for the Afghans.
1922 - Britain formally declares Egypt's independence, although still retaining control of the Suez Canal and the country's defence.
1931 - In Britain Sir Oswald Mosley formed the "New Party" which he said was dedicated to turning parliament "from a talk-shop into a workshop".
1941 - Alfonso XIII, ex-king of Spain, died in exile. After elections in 1931 which voted in the republicans, Alfonso refused to abdicate and was forced to leave Spain.
1942 - On the second day of the Battle of Java Sea two more Allied ships were sunk by the Japanese.
1943 - Nine Norwegian commandos sabotaged German heavy water installations near Ryukan in Norway.
1948 - The last British troops left India.
1952 - Vincent Massey took office as Governor-General of Canada, the first Canadian to hold the office.
1967 - Henry Luce, American publisher, died. He was a co-founder of Time magazine and also founded Life and Fortune.
1971 - The male voters of Liechtenstein defeat a referendum on giving women the vote.
1974 - A general election in Britain produced a minority Labour government under Harold Wilson.
1975 - In the worst underground train crash in Britain, 42 people died when a train crashed into the buffers at Moorgate station, London.
1986 - Swedish Prime Minister Olaf Palme was assassinated by a gunman in central Stockholm.
1991 - After 42 days of the Gulf War, U.S. and allied forces ceased fire at 8 a.m. Kuwait time and Iraq told its army to stop fighting.
1993 - The seige at Waco, Texas, began after the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco and Firearms tried to serve an arrest warrant for weapons charges on Branch Davidian sect leader David Koresh.
1994 - NATO jets shot down four warplanes violating Bosnia's no-fly zone.
1994 - Moldova's main independence party claimed a clear victory in the country's first post-Soviet parliamentary elections.
1996 - Calling it the saddest day of her life, Britain's Princess Diana agreed to divorce her estranged husband Prince Charles.
